breadcrumb: Hanging signs that use the overhead space
h1: Hanging signs that use the overhead space
lead: Hanging signs can make a destination visible when wall space is limited or when a message needs to be seen above surrounding activity. An interior department sign, a suspended reception marker and an exterior hanging identity are different projects with different support requirements. Vision Graphics can help New York businesses develop the artwork and format around the actual viewing direction. Start with the available overhead area, the message and the site’s restrictions, then review the supporting structure and placement before choosing a production approach.

sections.h2: Design for the angle of approach
sections.html: Determine whether the sign needs one readable face or two. Keep the message short enough to recognize while moving, and consider what sits behind the sign from each direction. A strong silhouette and clear contrast may be more useful than fine detail.

sections.h2: Treat suspension as part of the project
sections.html: Document ceiling or bracket conditions, clearances, access and any restrictions from the property team. The support system must be appropriate for the sign and location. Exterior exposure adds further considerations, so interior and exterior concepts should not share an assumed mounting specification.

items.p: Identify aisles, service areas or destinations from a distance.
Present the message to people approaching from opposite directions.
Explore a shaped or rectangular panel that fits the surrounding architecture.

items.q: Can a hanging sign be double-sided?
items.a_html: Yes, the layout can account for two approaches. Placement and support details still need review for the chosen format.

items.q: Can any ceiling support a sign?
items.a_html: No. The supporting structure and fixing method must be assessed for the site and sign.
